tasks.economic_output: ISF-10 transmitted to CBP at least 24 hours before lading: the ten importer data elements assembled from PO, packing list and booking, matched to the carrier's AMS bill of lading, with amendments filed as data changes; accepted when CBP returns an accepted status with no late or inaccurate flags.
tasks.notes: Form assembly with a $5,000 per-violation penalty; must be transmitted under the importer's or a licensed broker/forwarder's bond and ABI/AMS connection, so the filer gate remains. R anchored to underwriting-intake (0.94) minus 2.

tasks.name: Export control classification (ECCN) determination
tasks.economic_output: Written ECCN or EAR99 determination memo: CCL order of review, technical parameters compared against control thresholds, licence requirement by destination and end use, with rationale suitable for the export compliance file; accepted when the empowered official adopts it.
tasks.notes: Technical-parameter judgment with penalties of $300k+ per violation; R anchored between medical-coding (0.70) and legal-research-memo (0.65), discounted for spec ambiguity. Empowered official must sign; BIS CCATS remains the binding route.

tasks.name: Landed cost quote
tasks.economic_output: Per-unit landed cost quote for an import lane: product cost, ocean or air freight, insurance, duty by HTS, MPF and HMF, brokerage and inland delivery itemized with assumptions and validity date; accepted when the buyer uses it for a purchase or pricing decision.
tasks.notes: Arithmetic is checkable; the duty line inherits classification risk. R anchored to freight-quote (0.90) minus 5. Forwarders increasingly give this away inside instant quotes, so the price is already compressed.

tasks.name: Used vehicle appraisal report
tasks.economic_output: Written valuation report for one used vehicle: condition grading from inspection photos and history report, comparable sales, condition and mileage adjustments, stated value with methodology and appraiser attestation; accepted when a dealer, lender or insurer relies on the value.
tasks.notes: Valuation judgment on top of a physical inspection the AI cannot perform; R anchored to claims-damage-estimate-review (0.85) minus 7. Certified-appraiser signature is required for insurance, legal and diminished-value uses.

tasks.name: Auto repair estimate write-up
tasks.economic_output: Written repair estimate on the repair order: labor operations with guide times at the posted rate, parts with pricing and availability, sublet, shop supplies and tax, customer-facing explanation and authorization line; accepted when the service manager releases it to the customer unchanged.
tasks.notes: R anchored to claims-damage-estimate-review (0.85); labor guides and parts catalogs make the line items checkable. The technician's diagnosis remains the human input; the write-up is the service writer's deliverable.

tasks.name: Auto warranty claim submission
tasks.economic_output: OEM warranty claim coded and submitted from the repair order: labor op codes, causal part, complaint-cause-correction narrative, punch times and policy checks completed, claim submitted through the OEM portal and tracked to payment; accepted when the OEM pays without rejection or chargeback.
tasks.notes: OEM acceptance is a deterministic signal; R anchored to po-processing (0.95) minus 5 for narrative and coding judgment. Outsourced processors already advertise 97%+ first-submission rates, so the bar is high.

tasks.name: Deposition transcript summary
tasks.economic_output: Page-line deposition summary (topical or chronological) with key admissions flagged, accepted by the supervising attorney without material omissions
tasks.notes: R anchored to chart-summarization (0.90); page-line cites make omissions checkable. Market already AI-compressed (AI vendors at $1/page vs $3-10 human).

tasks.name: Medical records chronology
tasks.economic_output: Sourced chronological medical timeline (date, provider, diagnosis, treatment, page cite) with gaps and missing records flagged, accepted by the nurse reviewer or attorney
tasks.notes: R anchored to chart-summarization (0.90) less a few points for handwriting, poor scans and multi-provider records; offshore vendors already at $0.50-0.75/page.

tasks.name: Privilege log entries
tasks.economic_output: Rule 26(b)(5)-compliant log entries (date, author, recipients, privilege basis, non-revealing description) for 100 withheld documents, accepted by reviewing counsel
tasks.notes: R anchored to discovery-classification (0.92) less description-drafting judgment; attorney must confirm each privilege basis, waiver exposure keeps review mandatory.

tasks.name: Brief cite-check and Bluebook conformance
tasks.economic_output: Every citation verified against the primary source (quote, pin cite, subsequent history) and conformed to Bluebook, with a corrected table of authorities
tasks.notes: R anchored to nda-review (0.85): narrow rule-bound review, but only with retrieval access to primary sources; without a case-law database citation verification collapses.

tasks.name: Contract redline negotiation round
tasks.economic_output: One turn of tracked-changes redline responding to the counterparty draft, with an issues list and fallback positions the client attorney adopts
tasks.notes: Below nda-review (0.85) because a live round needs counterparty strategy and client priorities, not just playbook conformance; attorney signs off every turn.

tasks.name: Subpoena response package
tasks.economic_output: Objections and responses letter, collected and privilege-screened responsive documents, production log and custodian certification ready for attorney signature
tasks.notes: Blend of demand-letter (0.90) formulaic objections and discovery-classification (0.92) screening, discounted for scope judgment; attorney signature on objections is the legal gate.

tasks.name: AML suspicious activity report narrative
tasks.economic_output: FinCEN SAR narrative (who, what, when, where, why, how) plus populated structured fields from the investigated case, passing BSA officer QC without rework
tasks.notes: Set under kyc-review (0.88): regulator-facing prose where human first-pass QC approval is itself only 65-75%; BSA officer filing decision is the gate.

tasks.name: Transaction monitoring alert review
tasks.economic_output: Each L1 alert enriched, investigated and dispositioned (close or escalate to case) with a documented rationale that passes QC sampling
tasks.notes: R anchored to soc-alert-triage (0.88); 85-95% of alerts are false positives, so missed true positives carry the asymmetric cost and escalation sampling stays mandatory. Market already AI-compressed.

tasks.name: Sanctions screening hit disposition
tasks.economic_output: Each sanctions, PEP or watchlist name-match hit cleared or escalated with documented identifiers compared and rationale acceptable to OFAC-style audit
tasks.notes: Slightly above soc-alert-triage (0.88): structured identifier comparison with 85-99% false positives; strict-liability sanctions regime keeps escalation sampling mandatory.

tasks.name: Fraud case investigation report
tasks.economic_output: Desk investigation report: evidence gathered and cited, timeline, inconsistencies, database and OSINT findings, and a supported disposition recommendation the SIU lead accepts
tasks.notes: Open investigative synthesis, anchored near legal-research-memo (0.65) plus structure credit; wrongful fraud findings carry bad-faith exposure so a licensed or certified investigator signs.

tasks.name: Insurance subrogation demand package
tasks.economic_output: Pre-suit demand letter plus damages package (proof of payment, liability evidence, photos, reports, interest calc) the responsible carrier accepts as complete
tasks.notes: Between demand-letter (0.90) and insurance-policy-review (0.87): formulaic letter plus liability and damages judgment; subro adjuster reviews before it goes out.

tasks.name: Loss run analysis report
tasks.economic_output: Normalized multi-carrier, multi-year loss runs with frequency and severity trends, open reserves, large-loss narrative and renewal recommendations accepted by the broker or underwriter
tasks.notes: R anchored to insurance-policy-review (0.87) with underwriting-intake (0.94) as the extraction ceiling; carrier format variance is the main failure mode.

tasks.name: Investor pitch deck draft
tasks.economic_output: Investor-ready 12-15 slide seed or Series A deck draft (problem, solution, market, traction, model, team, financials, ask) built from founder inputs and styled to a template; accepted when the founder sends it to investors after a light edit rather than a rework pass
tasks.notes: R anchored to presentation-design (0.80) minus 2 points for investor-narrative judgment; agencies sell the story work, not the slides, so substitutability stays at 3.

tasks.name: Monthly investor update
tasks.economic_output: Monthly investor update memo or email: KPIs versus plan, highlights, lowlights, cash and runway, hiring, asks, drawn from the company dashboards and prior updates; accepted when the founder sends it with light edits
tasks.notes: R anchored to press-release (0.90) minus 5 points for metric accuracy risk; formulaic genre with a fixed template each month.

tasks.name: Cap table and dilution scenario model
tasks.economic_output: Spreadsheet model of the current cap table with pro forma ownership under 2-4 financing scenarios (SAFE and note conversion, option pool top-up, pro rata, priced round) tied to the source ledger; accepted when a fractional CFO or counsel signs off on the ownership percentages
tasks.notes: R anchored to financial-model (0.78) minus 3 points: arithmetic is checkable but pre-money vs post-money SAFE conversion and pool-shuffle mechanics are classic error traps.

tasks.name: Market sizing (TAM, SAM, SOM) analysis
tasks.economic_output: Top-down and bottom-up TAM, SAM and SOM sizing with sourced inputs, an editable calculation workbook and a 3-5 page writeup; accepted when an investor or product marketing lead carries the numbers into a deck without re-deriving them
tasks.notes: R anchored to market-research-memo (0.82) minus 2 points for source-quality judgment on the bottom-up inputs; deep-research products already sell this.

tasks.name: Term sheet summary and analysis
tasks.economic_output: Plain-English summary of a venture term sheet (valuation and option pool, liquidation preference, anti-dilution, pro rata, board and protective provisions, drag-along, vesting) benchmarked against NVCA and market norms with off-market terms and negotiation points flagged; accepted when founder counsel adopts it as the basis for the markup
tasks.notes: R anchored to nda-review (0.85) minus 3 points for term interplay; legally gated in practice since negotiation and signing stay with counsel, this prices the analysis memo only.

tasks.name: Quarterly board deck
tasks.economic_output: Quarterly board deck (financials versus plan, KPIs, variance commentary, pipeline, hiring, cash and runway, asks, appendix) assembled from the close package, CRM and prior decks; accepted when the CEO or CFO sends the pre-read with narrative edits only
tasks.notes: R anchored to presentation-design (0.80) minus 8 points for multi-source financial reconciliation; the CFO still owns every number shown to the board.

tasks.name: Competitive sales battlecard
tasks.economic_output: One-competitor battlecard: positioning, strengths and weaknesses, objection handling, landmine questions, pricing intel and win-loss themes sourced from public materials, review sites and call notes; accepted when product marketing publishes it to reps without rework
tasks.notes: R anchored to market-research-memo (0.82); factual claims about competitors need a PMM check, and Klue and Crayon already ship AI-generated battlecards.

tasks.name: Personalized product demo script
tasks.economic_output: Prospect-specific demo script and talk track: discovery recap, tailored use-case flow and click path, persona and data setup notes, objection prep and next-step close, built from CRM notes and prospect research; accepted when the SE or AE runs the demo from it with minor edits
tasks.notes: R anchored to outbound-sequence (0.88) minus 3 points for product-accuracy risk; environment and data setup stay human, so substitutability is 3.

tasks.name: Configured price quote (CPQ)
tasks.economic_output: Configured quote for a multi-line B2B deal: validated product and bundle configuration, list pricing, approved discount tiers, term and ramp schedule and a quote document ready for approval; accepted when it passes deal desk and finance without correction
tasks.notes: R anchored between policy-quote-generation (0.85) and requisition-review-100 (0.94); rule-driven against a price book, but messy catalogs and compatibility rules keep it under the deterministic-form tasks.

tasks.name: Deal desk discount approval review
tasks.economic_output: Deal desk review of a non-standard discount request: margin and floor check, comparable-deal lookup, policy and precedent check, term trade-offs, recommendation and approval routing memo; accepted when the approver signs off on the recommendation without reworking the analysis
tasks.notes: R anchored to requisition-review-100 (0.94) minus 9 points for judgment on precedent and trade-offs; approval authority stays with the human approver.

tasks.name: Brand messaging framework
tasks.economic_output: Messaging framework document: positioning statement, value pillars with proof points, audience-specific messages, tagline options, voice and tone guide and boilerplate, grounded in customer research inputs and competitor messaging; accepted when the marketing lead adopts it as the source of truth for copy
tasks.notes: R anchored to ad-creative (0.85) minus 10 points: taste-based acceptance plus stakeholder alignment, the part agencies charge for in workshops.

tasks.name: Influencer campaign brief
tasks.economic_output: Creator-facing campaign brief: objectives and KPIs, audience, key messages and mandatories, do and do-not list, deliverables by creator tier, posting schedule, FTC disclosure requirements, usage rights and approval flow; accepted when the agency or brand manager sends it to creators unchanged
tasks.notes: R anchored to press-release (0.90) minus 5 points; formulaic document, main rejection reason is brand-voice fit and missing disclosure or rights terms.

tasks.name: Product launch plan
tasks.economic_output: Launch plan: tiering, goals and KPIs, positioning and messaging summary, audience and channel plan, asset list with owners and dates, sales enablement plan, timeline, risk register and post-launch review plan; accepted when the product marketing lead runs the launch from it with owner edits only
tasks.notes: R anchored to proposal-drafting (0.80) minus 5 points for open-ended, org-specific sequencing; consultants price the cross-functional alignment, not the document.

tasks.name: Compensation benchmark report
tasks.economic_output: Market pay report for one role: matched survey benchmarks, percentile ranges, geographic and level adjustments, and a recommended range the comp lead accepts for use
tasks.notes: Job-matching judgment and licensed survey data gate quality; R set between donor-prospect-profile (0.65) and resume-screening (0.90).

tasks.name: Employee handbook update
tasks.economic_output: Revised handbook with policies updated for current federal, state and local law, a change log, and redlines the employer's counsel signs off on
tasks.notes: Multi-state law currency is the failure mode; attorney review remains the norm. R anchored below nda-review (0.85) because scope is broader.

tasks.name: Form I-9 compliance audit
tasks.economic_output: Audit of 100 Form I-9 files: every substantive and technical error flagged by field, missing or expired documents listed, correction instructions per USCIS procedure, and a summary report
tasks.notes: Rule-checkable form audit; R anchored to kyc-review (0.88) and access-recertification-review (0.86), slightly higher because the rule set is narrower. Corrections must be executed by the employer.

tasks.name: Performance review draft
tasks.economic_output: Written annual review draft from manager notes, goals and feedback: rated competencies with evidence, accomplishments, development areas, and next-cycle goals the manager finalizes
tasks.notes: Manager owns the ratings; AI drafts from supplied evidence. R anchored under job-description (0.95) because judgments must match documentation used in employment decisions.

tasks.name: Workplace investigation report
tasks.economic_output: Investigation report for one complaint: allegations, evidence and interview summaries, credibility analysis, findings against policy, and recommendations, defensible if litigated
tasks.notes: Interviews and credibility determinations stay human; report is usually attorney-reviewed for privilege. R anchored to legal-research-memo (0.65), lower for credibility findings.

tasks.name: Individualized Education Program (IEP) draft
tasks.economic_output: IDEA-compliant IEP draft: present levels from evaluation data, measurable annual goals, services and minutes, accommodations, and placement rationale, ready for the IEP team meeting
tasks.notes: Legally gated: the IEP team must meet and the parent must consent before the document takes effect; FERPA data handling. R anchored near legal-research-memo (0.65).

tasks.name: Lesson plan unit
tasks.economic_output: Standards-aligned 2 to 3 week instructional unit: unit plan, daily lesson plans, materials, differentiation notes, and formative and summative assessments a teacher adopts
tasks.notes: Marketplace (TpT, Tes) already prices units at tens of dollars; R anchored between course-module-dev (0.80) and quiz-generation (0.92).

tasks.name: Course syllabus
tasks.economic_output: Complete syllabus: learning outcomes mapped to program outcomes, weekly schedule, readings, assessment weights, grading rubric summary, and required institutional policy language
tasks.notes: Institutional policy text must be verbatim and outcome mapping is checkable; R anchored to quiz-generation (0.92), slightly lower for sequencing judgment.

tasks.name: Letter of recommendation
tasks.economic_output: Tailored recommendation letter draft from the recommender's notes: specific examples, comparative language, and fit to the program or role, ready for the recommender to edit and sign
tasks.notes: Recommender must attest and sign; fabricated specifics are the failure mode. R anchored to job-description (0.95) and donor-acknowledgement-letters (0.95), lower for personal detail.

tasks.name: Crisis communications statement
tasks.economic_output: Holding or response statement for an active issue: facts confirmed, legal exposure avoided, stakeholder-specific versions, and Q&A lines, approved by counsel and the executive
tasks.notes: Counsel and CEO approval gate release; AI draft is a starting point. R anchored below press-release (0.90) for legal and tone judgment.

tasks.name: Targeted media list
tasks.economic_output: Verified list of 50 to 150 journalists and outlets matched to the campaign's beat and geography: recent relevant coverage, contact details, pitch notes, and deliverability checked
tasks.notes: Contact data sits behind paid databases and stale emails are the failure mode; R anchored between donor-prospect-profile (0.65) and data-extraction (0.96).

tasks.name: Executive speech draft
tasks.economic_output: 15 to 30 minute keynote or all-hands speech in the executive's voice: structure, stories, data points checked, transitions and closing, through two revision rounds
tasks.notes: Voice matching and taste drive acceptance; multiple revision rounds are the norm. R anchored below press-release (0.90).

tasks.name: Internal communications announcement
tasks.economic_output: Employee-facing announcement package: leadership email, intranet post, manager talking points and FAQ, on brand and consistent with HR and legal guidance
tasks.notes: Routine announcements only; layoffs, M&A or incidents escalate to the crisis-statement class. R anchored to press-release (0.90).

tasks.name: Manuscript copyedit
tasks.economic_output: A tracked-changes copyedit of a book manuscript segment (grammar, usage, consistency, house style, light fact queries) plus a style sheet, accepted when the author or managing editor takes it into normal review rather than re-editing.
tasks.notes: R anchored below translation (0.88): mechanical fixes are near-deterministic but voice preservation and query judgment are where editors reject; style-sheet consistency across a full book is the scaffold's hard part.

tasks.name: Back-of-book index
tasks.economic_output: A publisher-ready back-of-book index for a ~300-page nonfiction title (main headings, subheadings, cross-references, locators tied to final pagination), accepted when the managing editor sends it to typesetting with only minor edits.
tasks.notes: R anchored between technical-manual (0.85) and transcript-to-feature (0.70): term extraction is checkable, but concept-level headings, granularity, and cross-reference judgment are where professional indexers reject machine indexes.

tasks.name: Closed captioning
tasks.economic_output: A timed, speaker-identified, 99%-accurate same-language caption file (SRT/SCC/VTT) with sound-effect tags and line-break conventions for one hour of recorded video, accepted when it passes the buyer's accuracy spot check.
tasks.notes: R anchored near translation (0.88): ASR plus LLM cleanup is near-deterministic on clean audio; the market is already AI-compressed (Rev, 3Play, Verbit sell AI tiers), so the human price overstates durable willingness to pay.

tasks.name: Subtitle translation
tasks.economic_output: Translated, timed subtitles for one hour of video into one target language, condensed to reading-speed and character-per-line limits with idiom and on-screen text handled, accepted when a native-speaker QC passes it without retiming or retranslation.
tasks.notes: R anchored below translation (0.88) because condensation to reading speed and timing constraints add a failure mode plain document translation lacks; major language pairs only.

tasks.name: Ebook conversion and formatting
tasks.economic_output: A validated EPUB and KDP-ready file set from a finished manuscript (styled headings, TOC, front and back matter, scene breaks, embedded images, metadata), accepted when it passes EPUBCheck and the store previewer with no layout fixes requested.
tasks.notes: R anchored to bom-validation-costing (0.85): validator checks are deterministic, visual QA across readers is the residual; the market is already compressed by Vellum, Atticus and $49 to $129 formatting shops.

tasks.name: Audiobook narration
tasks.economic_output: One finished hour of retail-ready narrated audio (correct pronunciations, consistent character voicing, ACX/Audible technical spec, edited and mastered), accepted when the rights holder approves it for distribution without re-recording.
tasks.notes: R anchored below logo-concepts (0.70): taste-based acceptance and character voicing gate fiction; AI voices are already sold (Audible Virtual Voice, KDP) so the human PFH price is compressing; tool_cost is the TTS API spend per finished hour.

tasks.name: Screenplay coverage report
tasks.economic_output: A 4 to 8 page coverage report on a feature screenplay (logline, synopsis, scored grid on premise, structure, character, dialogue, marketability, Pass/Consider/Recommend verdict, and actionable notes), accepted when the writer or development exec uses it in place of a paid reader's notes.
tasks.notes: R anchored to transcript-to-feature (0.70): synopsis and structural diagnosis are reliable, taste calls on voice and marketability are where readers disagree; AI coverage at $9 to $45 already sells, so the human price is compressing.

tasks.name: Custom song composition
tasks.economic_output: A 2 to 3 minute original personalized song (lyrics built from the buyer's story, composed melody, produced recording in the requested genre) with one lyric revision, accepted when the gift buyer approves it for delivery.
tasks.notes: R anchored below logo-concepts (0.70): purely taste-based acceptance, and buyers of Songfinch-style products are paying for a named human artist; generative music tools already undercut at $30 to $50 with add-ons.

tasks.name: Sheet music transcription
tasks.economic_output: Engraved, playable notation (piano or lead sheet with melody, chords, lyrics, or single-instrument tab) transcribed by ear from a 3 to 4 minute recording, delivered as PDF and MusicXML, accepted when a musician plays it against the recording and finds only cosmetic engraving fixes.
tasks.notes: R below technical-manual (0.85): audio-to-MIDI tooling handles solo piano well but dense mixes, voicings, and rhythmic notation choices are where transcribers reject; the scaffold is a tool pipeline (source separation, AMT, engraving) more than text generation.

tasks.name: Music sync licensing clearance
tasks.economic_output: A clearance package for one commercial recording in one production: identified publishing and master owners with splits, PRO and label lookups, usage description, quote requests sent to each rights holder, and a status tracker through to executed license, accepted when the music supervisor or attorney signs off the file.
tasks.notes: Legally gated: the license only exists once each rights holder consents, so the AI deliverable is the ownership research plus request package and follow-up, not the clearance itself; R anchored between nda-review (0.85) and legal-research-memo (0.65) because split data is often stale or conflicting.

tasks.name: Casting breakdown and shortlist
tasks.economic_output: A written character breakdown for one principal role plus a ranked shortlist of 8 to 15 candidates from submitted profiles and self-tapes with fit rationale and availability notes, accepted when the director and producer take the list into callbacks without asking the casting office to re-sift.
tasks.notes: R anchored to transcript-to-feature (0.70) minus a taste penalty: breakdown copy is reliable, shortlist judgment on performance in self-tapes is video-heavy and director-specific; casting directors also sell relationships and agent access that a shortlist does not replace.

tasks.name: Apparel tech pack
tasks.economic_output: A factory-ready technical package for one garment style (front and back flats with callouts, graded measurement spec with tolerances, bill of materials with trims and fabric, construction and stitch notes, label and packaging placement), accepted when the manufacturer quotes and samples from it without a clarification round.
tasks.notes: R anchored below technical-manual and bom-validation-costing (0.85): spec tables, BOM and construction notes are text-native, but vector flats with accurate callouts and grading judgment are where technical designers reject; a wrong spec costs a sample round.

tasks.name: Packaging copy and claims compliance review
tasks.economic_output: A marked-up compliance review of one product label and packaging (mandatory panel elements, nutrition or supplement facts format, ingredient and allergen statements, net quantity, claim substantiation flags against FDA and FTC rules, class-action risk notes) with a corrections list, accepted when the regulatory lead or counsel signs the label for print.
tasks.notes: R anchored between contract-compliance-audit (0.92) and nda-review (0.85), discounted for claims interpretation: panel-format checks against 21 CFR 101 are rule-based, but implied-claim and substantiation judgment is where consultants and counsel add the value; sign-off stays with a human because the label is the liability surface.

tasks.name: Medication reconciliation
tasks.economic_output: Reconciled medication list across home, admission and discharge sources with discrepancies flagged and resolved, accepted when a pharmacist or clinician signs it without re-doing the history
tasks.notes: Pharmacist or clinician sign-off is the gate (Joint Commission NPSG.03.06.01); R set between discharge-summary-drafting (0.85) and medical-coding (0.70) because omitted home meds are silent errors.

tasks.name: Patient education handout
tasks.economic_output: Plain-language, reading-level-checked patient handout for a condition, procedure or medication, accepted when a clinician reviewer approves it for distribution without rewriting
tasks.notes: R anchored to prior-auth-appeal-letter (0.86); clinical review is required by most health systems but is a fast check, health-literacy targets are checkable with readability tools.

tasks.name: Specialist referral letter
tasks.economic_output: Referral letter with reason for referral, relevant history, medications, results and specific question, accepted when the referring physician signs and the receiving practice does not bounce it for missing information
tasks.notes: Physician signature required; R anchored to ambient-soap-note (0.88), chart context is in the EHR so the failure mode is omission, not fabrication.

tasks.name: Utilization review case determination
tasks.economic_output: Medical necessity determination against MCG or InterQual criteria with cited clinical facts and a recommendation, accepted when the UR nurse or physician advisor adopts it without re-abstracting the chart
tasks.notes: Adverse determinations must be made by a licensed physician under state UR statutes and URAC rules, so the agent produces the case file and recommendation only; R set between prior-auth (0.88) and medical-coding (0.70).

tasks.name: OpenAPI specification from codebase
tasks.economic_output: Complete OpenAPI 3.x document generated from the service code with schemas, examples, auth and error responses, accepted when it validates, matches live endpoints under contract tests and the maintainers merge it
tasks.notes: R anchored to code-documentation (0.90) with a stronger verifier (spec lint plus contract tests); spec generators already compress the human market so V overstates durable willingness to pay.

tasks.name: CI pipeline configuration
tasks.economic_output: Working CI configuration (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI or similar) with build, test, lint, caching and artifact steps, accepted when the pipeline runs green on the default branch and the team merges it
tasks.notes: R anchored to terraform-module (0.85); a green run is a strong verifier, secrets and deploy permissions are the part a human still wires; retries are high because runner environments differ from local.

tasks.name: Database schema design
tasks.economic_output: Normalized relational schema with tables, keys, indexes, constraints and migration scripts for a new application, accepted when the lead engineer approves it in design review and migrations apply cleanly
tasks.notes: R set between etl-pipeline (0.72) and sql-report (0.85); migrations run deterministically but access-pattern and scaling judgment is what review catches, and schema mistakes are expensive to unwind later.

tasks.name: Performance profiling report
tasks.economic_output: Profiling report for one backend service with flame graphs, hot paths, query and allocation findings and ranked remediation, accepted when the owning team adopts the top recommendations
tasks.notes: R anchored to cloud-cost-optimization-report (0.80); needs a load-generation or prod-like environment, findings are verifiable after fixes land, workload context is the missing input.

tasks.name: Tenant screening report
tasks.economic_output: Consolidated applicant report with credit, eviction, criminal and income verification against the landlord's stated criteria, accepted when the FCRA-compliant screener releases it and the landlord acts on it
tasks.notes: R anchored to kyc-review (0.88); FCRA obligations (permissible purpose, accuracy, adverse-action notices) and fair-housing rules gate the release; bureau data fees are the cost floor and the market is already automated so V overstates durable willingness to pay.

tasks.name: Property tax assessment appeal
tasks.economic_output: Assessment appeal package with comparable sales analysis, equity comps, valuation argument and completed county filing, accepted when it is filed on time and the assessor or review board hears it
tasks.notes: R anchored to cma-report (0.85) less a filing and hearing step; most firms work on contingency (25-50% of first-year savings) so the observed fee is a share of savings, not a price for the work; some states require a registered tax consultant or attorney to appear at hearings.

tasks.name: Rent roll audit
tasks.economic_output: Unit-by-unit tie-out of the rent roll to executed leases, ledgers, deposits and bank collections with a variance log, accepted when the acquisition or lender team relies on it without re-pulling the files
tasks.notes: R set between lease-abstraction (0.92) and audit-workpaper-prep (0.75); the tie-out is checkable but scanned lease files and ledger exports are messy, and missed concessions or side letters are underwriting losses.
